[[PDRM FA|PDRM]] | attendance = 178,443 (matches played behind closed doors are not included) | average attendance = 9,914 (matches played behind closed doors are not included) | prevseason = [[2019 Malaysia Super League|2019]] | nextseason = [[2021 Malaysia Super League|2021]] | updated = | season = [[2020 in Malaysian football|2020]] }} The '''2020 Malaysia Super League''' ({{langx|ms|Liga Super Malaysia 2020}}), known as the [[CIMB|CIMB Bank]] Liga Super Malaysia 2020 for sponsorship reasons, was the 17th season of the [[Malaysia Super League]], the top-tier professional [[association football|football]] league in Malaysia. [[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]] were the defending champions, having won their sixth title the [[2019 Malaysia Super League|previous season]]. The first transfer window was from 16 January to 15 March 2020. On 13 March 2020, it was announced that the league would be suspended indefinitely, due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. On 17 July, it was announced that the league would resume in August{{Cite web |date=2020-07-17 |title=Liga Malaysia 2020 to restart on 26 August |url=https://www.aseanfootball.org/v3/liga-malaysia-2020-to-restart-on-26-august/ |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=AFF - The Official Website Of The Asean Football Federation |language=en-US}} dependent on the situation at the time. Due to time constraints, the home-and-away format has been scrapped. Teams played each other only once, meaning that the champion of the Super League was decided after eleven rounds of matches.{{cite web|url=https://www.nst.com.my/sports/football/2020/05/588984/september-restart-m-league|title=September restart for M-League|publisher=nst.com.my|date=1 May 2020}} ==Teams== ===Changes from last season=== [[Kuala Lumpur FA|Kuala Lumpur]] and [[PKNP F.C.|PKNP]] are relegated to the [[2020 Malaysia Premier League|Malaysia Premier League]] after finishing bottom and second-bottom respectively in [[2019 Malaysia Super League|last season's Malaysia Super League]]. [[Sabah F.C. (Malaysia)|Sabah]] and [[PDRM FA|PDRM]] are promoted after securing their place as champions and 3rd-placed finishers in [[2019 Malaysia Premier League|last season's Malaysia Premier League]] (runners-up [[Johor Darul Ta'zim II F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim II]] is ineligible for the Super League due to being the reserve team to Johor Darul Ta'zim). As [[PKNS F.C.|PKNS]] has changed their status as the reserve team to [[Selangor FA|Selangor]], they are therefore replaced by the 5th-placed finishers of last season's Malaysia Premier League [[UiTM F.C.|UiTM]] (4th-placed finishers [[Terengganu FC II|Terengganu II]] is ineligible for the Super League due to being the reserve team to Terengganu FC). ====Team changes==== '''Promoted from the [[2019 Malaysia Premier League]]''' * [[Sabah F.C.
